title: Function value
parts: The output of the function f at input 3.
note: The brackets give an input. They do not imply multiplication by 3.

title: Root of a function
parts: Find input values where the function has output zero.
example: If f(x)=x²−4, the roots are x=−2 and x=2.
note: Roots are x-coordinates where the graph meets the horizontal axis.
wrong: Find the value of f at the input x=0.

title: Intersection of two function graphs
parts: Find inputs where both functions give the same output.
example: If f(x)=2x and g(x)=x+3, they meet when x=3 and the shared output is 6.
note: Equality at a specific x does not make the functions identical.
wrong: f and g have the same output at every input.

title: Inverse function
parts: The unique input to the invertible function f that produces y.
note: An inverse undoes the function. A reciprocal divides one by its value.

title: Completed square form
parts: The quadratic has its vertex at (h,k).
note: The sign of a determines whether the vertex is a minimum or maximum.

title: Stationary point
parts: The tangent to f at input a has slope zero.
example: For f(x)=x², f′(0)=0 and the graph has a minimum there.
note: A zero derivative can also occur without a local maximum or minimum, as for x³ at zero.
wrong: The graph must cross the horizontal axis at x=a.

title: Derivative from first principles
parts: The derivative is the limit of the average rate over a step h as that step approaches zero.
example: For f(x)=x², the ratio simplifies to 2x+h for h≠0, then approaches 2x.
note: Simplify or take the limit. Directly setting h=0 in the original ratio gives 0/0.
wrong: Set h=0 in the fraction before evaluating.
